business_problem: As BBVA expanded the number and diversity of AI and ML solutions across the bank, it needed a more flexible, scalable, and automated MLOps architecture that improved code reuse, reproducibility, version control, and lifecycle automation while preserving strict governance, risk management, and auditability.
solution_summary: BBVA evolved its ADA global data and AI platform on AWS to industrialize machine learning development and deployment across the bank. Users start from an ADA catalog template that creates a new project and captures regulatory metadata such as model description, business owner, and model tier. The platform automatically provisions a dedicated GitHub repository with standardized code scaffolding for training, model registration, metrics, and metadata. Amazon SageMaker AI provides the core ML workflow foundation for training, batch inference, monitoring, and reusable pipeline components, while ephemeral pull-request environments let teams validate changes in isolated sandboxes before merge. GitHub Actions manages CI/CD transitions across development and production branches. SageMaker Model Registry enforces lifecycle stages and approval states, while Amazon EventBridge and AWS Lambda automate approval workflows, promotions, and production registration. ADA also notifies BBVA’s risk portal on key lifecycle events to keep governance and audit processes synchronized.

data_flow: A user selects an ADA MLOps template, which captures regulatory metadata and provisions a GitHub repository with standardized scaffolding. Teams build and test training, batch inference, and monitoring pipelines on Amazon SageMaker AI, including ephemeral pull-request sandboxes created by GitHub Actions. Models, metrics, and metadata are registered in SageMaker Model Registry, then GitHub Actions, Amazon EventBridge, and AWS Lambda coordinate approvals, promotion, and production registration while notifying BBVA’s risk platform.
integration_points: repository branches mapped to development and production environments
business_outcome: BBVA standardized and automated ML delivery across business units, enabling faster experimentation, parallel development, stronger traceability, and embedded governance in a regulated banking environment.
metrics: 40% to 55% reduction in costs across pilot use cases
architecture_clues: Ephemeral pull-request environments provision isolated temporary training pipelines and model packages
Automated cleanup stops executions, deletes model versions, removes pipeline definitions, and cleans up model package groups
Model lifecycle stages are Development, QA, PreProduction, and Production
Auto-approval is allowed when a production-approved model is retrained without material pipeline changes
